section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Wave Superposition
section_1.content: Briefly recall how light waves interfere. Use an animation showing two coherent waves overlapping to create constructive and destructive interference patterns.
section_1.example: Visualize two ripples in a pond merging; where peaks meet, the water rises higher (constructive); where a peak meets a trough, the water stays flat (destructive).

section_2.title: Diffraction: Bending Around Barriers
section_2.content: Define diffraction as the phenomenon where waves spread out after passing through an aperture or around an obstacle. Focus on the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern.
section_2.example: Imagine a cat peering through a tiny slit in a door; the light waves 'bend' and spread into the room, revealing that light behaves like a wave, not just a straight-line particle.

section_3.title: The Holographic Recording Process
section_3.content: Explain the two-beam interference technique. A coherent laser beam is split into a reference beam and an object beam. Their interference pattern is captured on a photographic plate (the hologram).
section_3.example: Think of a security scanner: the reference beam acts as the 'standard,' while the object beam 'scans' the 3D surface. The resulting pattern on the plate is the 'coded' data of the object.

section_4.title: Reconstruction: Decoding the Wavefront
section_4.content: Explain how illuminating the hologram with the original reference beam diffracts the light to reconstruct the original wavefront, creating a 3D virtual image.
section_4.example: Like playing a vinyl record where the groove represents the 'interference pattern'; shining the light is the 'needle' that brings the 3D 'music' (image) back to life.

section_5.title: Summary and Real-World Application
section_5.content: Conclude by emphasizing that holography is essentially 'frozen' diffraction interference. Connect this to modern technology.
section_5.example: Discuss how credit card security holograms work: they are complex diffraction gratings that reveal different images depending on the viewing angle, making them nearly impossible to forge.
